title: Niryasa 5. The Hearing of Srila Jiva Gosvami's Letters and the Meeting with Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosvami
html:
Ramachandra explains to the king why Jiva wrote to them: the Gopala-champu and its inner meaning — parakiya; Vyasa Chakravarti takes it as svakiya; Ramachandra, Govinda and Narottama write to Vrindavana, and Jiva replies: "what is contemplated in sadhana, that is attained"; Mahaprabhu's meeting with Gopala Bhatta at Shrirangam and His prediction about Srinivasa; the Gopala-bhattashtaka

1Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya, glory to Nityananda!
Glory to Advaita-chandra, glory to Gaura's devotees!

2Then the king, clasping the feet of Sri Ramachandra,
began to speak sweet words:

3"What Prabhu said to you earlier1
I heard with my own ears:

4why did the Gosvamis write to you? —
make me blessed, let me hear it."

5Then Ramachandra says: "Hear the reason
why Sri Jiva wrote to us.

6Once Sri Jiva Gosvami
carefully sent my Prabhu the Gopala-champu.

7Seeing the book, my Prabhu rejoiced at heart:
'What a book full of rasa the Gosani has made!

8In the book he has described the pure parakiya-lila.'
Seeing this, my Prabhu was very happy.

9Not knowing the deep heart of Sri Rupa,2
people explain the verses by their outward sense as svakiya;

10no one can enter the inner meaning:
he has wholly described the pure parakiya-lila.

11He has revealed a book of rasa, the essence of nectar —
'How wondrous, how wondrous!' (Prabhu) said again and again.

12As if someone, finding a great jewel somewhere,
were to hide it in a casket —

13what is inside no one can see;
they see the casket — what concern have they with the treasure?

14What treasure is hidden, only he who hid it knows;
other people know only of the casket.

15Such is the Gosani's most profound conclusion:
(only) a steadfast devotee enters into it.

16This extract — the truth of rasa — no one understands;
therefore my Prabhu told everyone —

17"Let (no one) look at this book," he said firmly.3

18From then on he worships that book daily:
no one can understand its inner meaning.

19By the will of fate Sri Vyasa Chakravarti,
seeing that book, changed his opinion.

20Understanding nothing of the inner meaning,
he understood the outer meaning — as svakiya.

21Earlier he had been very learned,
but by the will of fate his opinion changed.

22Once, when my Prabhu was in Yajigrama,
he told my brother to describe Krishna's pastimes.

23He described the rasa of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna;
by the virtues of his rasa-filled verses the ears are soothed.

24He described the pure parakiya-lila,
tasting which people became mad with prema.

25At Kheturi, together with Thakura Mahashaya,
relishing the padas, he floats on the waves of prema.

26I, his brother, staying with them,
joyfully spoke of the rasa of Krishna.

27At that time Sri Vyasa Chakravarti came there,
and the four of us stayed together day and night.

28Then he raised a certain dispute,
and hearing it I was greatly pained at heart.

29(He said:) 'Tell me, what is your practice of constant remembrance?
How do you perform it — tell me in detail.'

30Then we told him the method of remembrance;
hearing it, he was somewhat put out.

31Then he said: 'You worship in parakiya —
but attainment is in svakiya; hear this:

32such are the incomparable words of Sri Jiva;
there is evidence for this word.

33You do not understand the heart of my Prabhu4 —
this I tell you for certain.'

34Hearing this, the three of us deliberated:
'Can Prabhu have revealed his heart to him?'

35The doubt in our minds grew greatly;
'What are we to do?' we thought day and night.

36'Sadhana one thing and attainment another — how can that be?'
All the time we wondered in our hearts: whom shall we ask?

37My brother had composed padas in the spirit of parakiya
and intended to spread them in Gauda.

38Thinking thus, the three of us deliberated
and, reflecting, firmly resolved:

39we three decided to write a letter
and send it to Sri Jiva Gosani —

40one letter to the companions of the Gosvami;
and we considered: who will carry it?

41There was a maha-bhagavata named Raya Vasanta,
who was always thinking of going to Vrindavana.

42We told him everything in detail,
and through him we three sent the letter:

43'To Sri Jiva Gosvami and all his companions,
to all those great souls, tell everything.'

44Taking the letter, the Raya went to Vrindavana
and, coming to the feet of Sri Gosvami, gave him the letter;

45then he took the letter to the companions
and told them everything in detail.

46After some days the Gosani sent an answer;
the companions, taking the letter, quickly returned.

47One letter the Gosani wrote to my Prabhu:
in it he speaks of Vyasa with displeasure.

48With feeling the Gosvami (writes) in this letter:
'Where is Vyasa Sharma now?

49Be sure to write me about this:
I cannot understand what is in his mind.'

50And then the Gosvami's letter to us:
a most wondrous letter, a nectar for the ears.

51'What need is there to write to me,
when you are vessels of the mercy of Srimat Acharya?

52The Acharya Mahashaya has instructed you especially;
his opinion is my opinion.

53What is contemplated in sadhana, that is what is attained' —
this he explained in the letter, without any doubt.

54This truth Sri Gosani Krishnadasa
revealed in his book:

55"Whoever worships, taking up some bhava of Vraja,
obtains a body suited to that bhava and attains Krishna in Vraja."5

56This is the whole essence, stated unshakeably.
Hear the Gosvami's letter — hearing it is auspicious.

57First, the Gosvami's letter to my Prabhu;
in it — listen — your name too appears.

58When Raya Vasanta went to Vrindavana,
the Gosani asked him about my Prabhu.

59Sri Raya Vasanta gave him all the news,
and the Gosani learned everything that had happened.

60First he sent a letter to my Prabhu;
receiving the letter, my Prabhu placed it on his head.

61From the letter Prabhu learned all the news;
reading the letter, Prabhu shed streams of tears.

62Then, when the Raya returned to Gauda,
we, receiving the letter, were greatly pleased.

63I asked him about everything:
"Why does the Gosvami's letter speak of Sharma's words?"

64The Raya says: "When the Gosani heard the reason, (he said:)
'Who but Sharma could have said such a thing?

65Such words never come from a devotee's mouth:
this is surely the opinion of a brahmana pandita.'"

66The Gosvami's letter to Prabhu was in the month of Bhadra;
and in Vaishakha — the letter to us. Listen.

67Here is the letter: "May it be well. To the feet of Sri Sri Srinivasa Acharya, whose two feet give me all happiness — the one named Jiva, bowing, submits. I always wish for your welfare; for many days no news has come from there — so let us be gladdened. Here I am at present in good bodily health, and the others likewise; but the feet of Sri Bhugarbha Gosvami have left the body, consciously surrendering the soul to Sri Vrindavana-natha — this is the special news. Write of the welfare of your companions, especially of Sri Vrindavana Dasa — whether he studies a little or not. And further: where and how is Sri Vyasa Sharma now? Write also of Sri Vasudeva Kaviraja. Moreover, the corrections of the 'Rasamrita-sindhu', the 'Madhava-mahotsava', the 'Uttara-champu' and the 'Hari-namamrita' are not yet quite finished, and because of the rains we are not sending them now; later, if fate is favourable, they will be sent. Know that all here offer you obeisances as befits; and convey my obeisances to those there. Bhadra, the bright fortnight."6

68(The letter to us:) "To Sri Raja Mahashaya — auspicious blessings. May it be well. To Sri Ramachandra Kaviraja, Sri Narottama Dasa and Sri Govinda Dasa, praised by all Vaishnavas — the abode of happiness and wealth for such as me — I, named Jiva, from Sri Vrindavana, with an embrace, submit. I especially wish for your welfare there; having received a letter full of affection, I long for one again and again. The beautiful songs which you lovingly sent — from them I at once obtained great good; what more need be said to those who love without motive? As for what you constantly ask — the method of constant remembrance — it is clearly stated in the 'Sri Rasamrita-sindhu': 'service in the form of the practitioner' and so on. There 'in the form of the practitioner' means 'with the external body', and 'in the perfected form' means 'with the body contemplated as suited to one's own desired service'. And there service in the perfected form is only according to the path of raganuga; its varieties according to time, place and lila are many — how much can be written? Service in the form of the practitioner, however, is to be understood according to the method of vaidhi, following the Agamas and the rest. Srimat Acharya Mahashaya will instruct you especially in this; for this is indeed our all; what more is there to add? The fourteenth day of Vaishakha."7

69(A third letter:) "To the most worshipful ones, whose mind-bee is plump and intoxicated with drinking the unobstructed nectar of the lotus feet of Sri Govinda, whose lives are purified by study of the instructions to Vaishnavas, whose whole hearts are nourished by tasting the nectar of the feet of the assembly of like-minded sadhus — a request, with obeisance and embrace, from one who is drowning in the ocean of samsara. Since I am far away and deprived of your sight, consider how my joyful fortune may arise: for you are the helmsman on the ocean of reflection on living in the highest good company. The beautiful songs composed on the pastimes of Sri Radha and Krishna have been received; and see to whatever else is fitting. Let the honoured ones learn the method of sadhana from the letter of Srimat Gosvami. The fragrance of the garland of poems, borne by the gentle breeze from the sandal-hill — Sri Govinda, king of poets — connected with the moon Krishna, intoxicating the bees who have taken shelter at the feet of the wish-fulfilling tree Srimat Jiva, has caused wonder in everyone in the forests of Vraja — what could be higher? This is a brief letter."8

70Hearing the letters, the maharaja was filled with boundless joy:
gooseflesh and trembling all over his body, streams of tears from his eyes.

71Faltering in bhava, the king fell to the ground
and suddenly, crying out, rose up.

72Clasping Ramachandra's feet, he weeps;
Ramachandra, raising him, embraced him tightly.

73With arms round each other's necks, both weep loudly,
again and again crying only, "Alas, alas!"

74"You are fortunate, O king, calm your heart:
Prabhu's mercy has come to you as it should."

75Then the king says: "Listen, sir:
you are merciful for the sake of my deliverance.

76From you I have received the teaching on rasa;
now I have fully understood the opinion of my Prabhu.

77You are a maha-bhagavata; by your mercy
I have firmly come to know the pure bhava of Vraja."

78Ramachandra says: "Hear my word:
I have told you the essence of this conclusion.

79Keep it hidden in your heart;
let it never be divulged elsewhere.

80You, maharaja, are the crown of the wise:
understand it yourself in your heart.

81And I tell you one thing more, listen, O king:
giving up jnana and karma, relish bhava.

82By jnana, karma and the like this is never attained —
this I have told you for certain."

83Then the king again addresses Ramachandra:
"Be merciful and tell me — let my doubt be dispelled.

84Tell me now of the meeting of Bhatta Gosvami:
how did he come to see Mahaprabhu?"

85Ramachandra says: "Listen, O king, I shall tell you;
I speak to you — be attentive.

86(The Lord) toured the holy places of the South9 —
all this is written in the Chaitanya-charitamrita:

87in the Madhya-khanda, see the ninth chapter,
and relish the pilgrimage to the South.

88There (the author) did not name the name openly —
he kept it secret and did not divulge it;

89but he wrote there one word of essence —
hear the essence of that account.

90In the Chaitanya-charitamrita this is revealed:
there he surely wrote of the Gosvami's meeting:

91'A certain Sri Vaishnava named Venkata Bhatta
respectfully invited Prabhu;

92bringing Him to his house, he washed His feet
and drank that water with his whole family.'10

93Briefly he expressed this word;
I shall tell you what happened — be attentive.

94Mahaprabhu, touring the holy places of the South,
suddenly came to Sri Ranga-kshetra.

95In that holy place lived the best of the brahmanas of Telingana —
his name was Sri Trimalla Bhatta, (head of) the brahmana community.11

96Having bathed at midday, Prabhu came to his house;
seeing Him with his family, (he) was filled with prema.

97Bowing many times, he washed His feet
and drank the water from His feet together with his family.

98Seating Him on a worthy seat, he entreated Him much:
"Be merciful, Prabhu, we take shelter."

99Pleased, Prabhu stayed there
and in great bliss took His meals in his house.

100Carefully taking Mahaprabhu's remnants,
he partook of that prasada with his family.

101Receiving the prasada, all floated in bliss;
after the meal they offered Prabhu mukhavasa.

102Humbly falling at Prabhu's feet,
with joined palms he entreats:

103"Prabhu, now the four months of the rains have come;
sannyasis do not tour the holy places at this time.

104If out of mercy You stay for these four months,
there will be jubilation in our hearts."

105Pleased, Prabhu gave His consent;
hearing this, all were greatly glad.

106Mahaprabhu stayed in his house;
in great bliss the Bhatta serves Him.

107Bathing in the Kaveri, seeing Ranganatha,
always kirtana and dancing with the devotees —

108there He stayed, having reached the limit of happiness;
thus the four months passed.

109Venkata's boy, named Sri Gopala Bhatta,
guilelessly served the abode of Gaura (Gauranga).

110His father, knowing his good character,
gladly set him to attend on Him.

111For four months he served in countless ways —
it cannot all be told in detail.

112A golden complexion, great learning, sweet speech,
his whole body beautiful, overflowing with streams of loveliness.

113What wondrous sweetness of body!
His form is most sweet — with what shall I compare it?

114Arms long, reaching to the knees, navel deep,
magnanimous, of composed character,

115eyes surpassing the lotus, chest high,
palms and soles red.

116Knowing in his heart Mahaprabhu's wishes,
he joyfully fulfilled them before He spoke.

117Seeing the expertise of his service, Prabhu was pleased:
"How did he know what was in My mind?"

118Saying this, Mahaprabhu was pleased
and showed mercy to the whole family, the servants and maids.

119One day Mahaprabhu lay down to rest,
and Bhatta Gosani serves His feet.

120Prabhu was greatly pleased with the service of His feet
and in private began to say something to him:

121"Listen, Gopala: you are a companion of Radha."
The Bhatta says: "And You are the son of the king of Vraja;

122taking Radhika's bhava, You have descended:
leaving Your dark colour, You have now become golden."

123Saying this, in the special bhava of the two
both revealed their natural bhava.

124When both, returning to outward consciousness, grew calm,
Prabhu spoke to him sweetly:

125"For some days serve your father and mother,
and then go to Vrindavana.

126In Vrindavana, together with Sri Rupa and Sanatana,
you will find many waves of happiness."

127Saying this, Mahaprabhu, pleased,
graciously gave him a kaupina and an outer cloth.12

128Taking the kaupina and outer cloth on his head,
he bowed many times, prostrate on the ground.

129Then Mahaprabhu, placing His foot on his head,
raised him and embraced him.

130Prabhu said: "Listen, I shall tell you something:
carry out this order of Mine without fail.

131From Gauda will come a young brahmana:
know for certain — he is My shakti.

132His name is Srinivasa; when I am no longer seen,
he will come to Vrindavana while still young.

133This kaupina and outer cloth you will give to him,
and, giving him hundreds of thousands of verses (of books), you will send him to Gauda.

134Tell Sanatana and Rupa all this,
so that they entrust to him the books on the pastimes of Vraja.

135He is My own shakti, and not otherwise;
all these secrets you must tell them."

136Saying, "As You command," he bowed his head to His feet
and, prostrate on the ground, bowed to His feet.

137Prabhu said: "And I tell you one thing more:
having toured the holy places of the South, I shall soon return.

138Then you will go to Vrindavana;
I shall send a seat and a cord for you.

139Sitting on that seat, you will put the cord round your neck
and show mercy to Srinivasa, the embodiment of prema.

140Tell him the essence of these words:
'Your mercy is My mercy — what more to say?'"13

141The cloth and things given by Prabhu he carefully
hid and kept in deep secrecy.

142When Sri Bhatta Gosani went to Vrindavana,
he lived together with Sri Rupa and Sanatana.

143Of this, in the Chaitanya-charitamrita,
Kaviraja Gosani has clearly told.

144When he described the branches of Mahaprabhu,
there — listen — are these words:

145"Sri Gopala Bhatta is one branch, most excellent,
whose talks of prema were with Rupa and Sanatana."14

146Gosvami Krishnadasa, in a hymn to Bhatta Gosani,
revealed all this:

147"He who has the power to proclaim Hari-bhakti unceasingly,
who always experiences the true and is detached from the worldly,

148whose seat is renowned through the coming of Mahaprabhu —
who can understand this play of Chaitanya?

149Such is his good fortune that it cannot be told:
in his house Prabhu joyfully stayed.

150May that Gopala Bhatta
always shine in my heart — this is my desire.

151From his eyes tears flow unceasingly,
sweat streams over his holy body all the time;

152abundant gooseflesh and trembling — unceasingly;
his voice falters as he utters the name.

153As soon as his tongue utters the name 'Hare Krishna',
he unceasingly makes the sounds 'Ha-ha, ha-ha, ha-ha'.

154As soon as he says this, he loses consciousness.
May that Gopala cast his merciful glance upon me.

155The one known in Vrindavana as Sri Guna Manjari —
that is Gopala Bhatta, equal to her in sweetness —

156out of mercy to the people of Kali he descended,
tasted madhurya-rasa and spread it.

157Tasting that sweet rasa,
he showed mercy to living beings in order to distribute it.

158He who ever abides in the rasa of prema-bhakti,
who relished it in many ways,

159who is expert in the distinctions of ashraya, rati and rasa,
who truly told of them as they deserve" —

160thus, beginning with this, the virtues of Bhatta Gosvami
Kaviraja Gosani described.

161Here is (the hymn): "He who is mighty in proclaiming Hari-bhakti unceasingly, who always experiences the truth and is detached from the transient, whose seat is renowned through the blessed coming of the best of Lords — may Gosvami Gopala Bhatta shine in my heart. (1) He who in the land of Vraja is renowned under the name Guna Manjari, who was sent (by the Lord), manifesting compassion for the people of Kali, to spread the special bliss of madhurya-rasa — may Gosvami Gopala Bhatta shine in my heart. (2) Beautiful with unceasing streams of tears and sweat, full of abundant gooseflesh, trembling and stupor, uttering the name, his heart losing itself on the syllables 'Hari, ha, ha, ha' — may Gosvami Gopala Bhatta shine in my heart. (3) He who, tasting the sweetness of his own bhava abiding in Vraja, is intoxicated — dances, laughs, sings, full of mad emotions, yet at the order to deliver the people of Kali turns his gaze outward — may Gosvami Gopala Bhatta shine in my heart. (4) He who knows the meaning of the verses (on bhakti), who is able to taste the distinctions of rati and rasa — whoever reads this chief jewel among hymns, which destroys all darkness, will merge into the group of manjaris. (5)"15

162This hymn dispels all darkness;
among hymns it is foremost and abundant (in blessing).

163Whoever reads it with a concentrated heart
suddenly attains a place in the group of manjaris.

164Whoever reads it properly
will surely attain the service of Radha and Krishna.

165Sanatana Gosani composed the Hari-bhakti-vilasa —
in it the same thing is revealed:

166the Hari-bhakti-vilasa, which the Gosani composed,
he credited in every place to Bhatta Gosvami.16

167By this he showed that they were one body;
whoever knows this is a great and steadfast devotee.

168The Gosvami composed the book Vaishnava-toshani —
in it there are these words, a stream of nectar:

169"Especially nourished by prema for Radha and Krishna
are Sri Gopala Bhatta and Raghunatha Dasa…"

170…if these two become my helpers,
shall I not become fully perfect?'

171Hear the evidence of this — I shall tell you;
listen attentively, with a concentrated heart:

172"Sri Gopala Bhatta and Raghunatha Dasa, especially nourished by prema for Radha's Beloved — whoever has these two as helpers even once, who is there that will not attain his goal and become fully perfect?"17

173And hear one thing more:
all these accounts are a nectar for the ears.

174Here is the evidence spoken by the ancients: "I bow to Gopala Bhatta, whose heart is flooded with the prema of Sanatana, who is marked by friendship with Sri Rupa, whose only life is Radha-ramana, and who grants the desire of those who worship."18

175Whoever sees between these three even a sesame seed of difference,
for that offence there is no deliverance.

176Whose body is full of the prema of Sanatana Gosani —
who will understand all these secrets?

177Whose friendship was with Sri Rupa —
for this he is renowned in all the world;

178whose only life is Sri Radha-ramana —
to the feet of such a Gosvami, millions of obeisances.

179Daivakinandana composed the Vaishnava-vandana19
and wrote these words in it:

180'I shall honour Gopala Bhatta in Vrindavana,
who always abides with Rupa and Sanatana.'

181These words are known everywhere:
people regard the three as one, believing this.

182Thus I have told of Bhatta Gosvami,
by hearing of whom the waves of prema increase.

183Now I shall tell of Prabhu's vow,
by hearing of which the pain of the heart departs.

184I shall tell you, brother, the essence of the words:
carefully put on your neck the necklace of nine jewels."

185Saying this, he recited the nine jewel-verses;
hearing them, the king was greatly pleased.

186This narrative of the Karnananda is an extract of nectar:
at its touch on the ear, the joy of prema is born in the devotees.

187The daughter of Sri Acharya Prabhu is Srila Hemalata:
has not the Creator fashioned a wish-fulfilling creeper of prema?

188Her two lotus feet sport in my heart;
Yadunandana Dasa tells the rasa of the Karnananda.

Thus ends the fifth niryasa of the Sri Karnananda, called "The Hearing of Srila Jiva Gosvami's Letters and the Meeting with Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosvami".

Notes

  1. Srinivasa (4.37–38).
  2. That is, the teaching of Rupa, whom Jiva followed; below (10) the subject is again the Gopala-champu.
  3. A single half-line (without rhyme). The sense: Srinivasa did not let the uninitiated read the book.
  4. Vyasa insinuates that Srinivasa shares the svakiya view.
  5. CC Madhya 8.222.
  6. Srila Jiva Gosvami's letter to Srinivasa (Sanskrit prose). These letters are also given by other sources — the Prema-vilasa (the Half-vilasa, letters) and the Bhakti-ratnakara (14) — with variants; cf. ev-jiva-srinivasa-letters. The Uttara-champu is the second part of the Gopala-champu.
  7. Jiva's letter to Ramachandra, Narottama and Govinda. The first line (shri-raja-mahashayeshu shubhashishah) stands in the edition like a heading; it may be an addition to the king (Vira Hambira). Jiva's answer is in substance Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 1.2.295 with his own commentary: service in the siddha-deha follows the raganuga path, external service the rules of vaidhi; he does not speak directly of svakiya or parakiya and refers them to Srinivasa's instruction. "What is contemplated in sadhana, that is attained" (53) is Ramachandra's conclusion.
  8. The third letter (its author is not named — "one drowning in the ocean of samsara"; from the sense, someone in Jiva's circle in Vrindavana) seems to be addressed to Govinda Kaviraja: it praises his songs and refers to the Gosvami's letter. The text in the edition is corrupt in places; translated by sense.
  9. In the edition the subject is "Sri Rupa", which is clearly an error: the reference is to Mahaprabhu's journey to the South (CC Madhya 9).
  10. CC Madhya 9.82–83. The author holds that Krishnadasa Kaviraja "did not name" Gopala Bhatta openly (according to tradition, Gopala Bhatta himself asked not to be mentioned in the CC).
  11. A divergence: according to the CC (Madhya 9.82), the Lord stayed with Venkata Bhatta; here the host is Trimalla Bhatta, and Gopala is "Venkata's boy" (109). According to tradition (cf. Bhakti-ratnakara 1), Venkata, Trimalla and Prabodhananda were three brothers, and Gopala the son of Venkata; cf. the Prema-vilasa glossary.
  12. According to tradition (cf. Bhakti-ratnakara 1, Prema-vilasa), Mahaprabhu later sent Gopala Bhatta His kaupina, cloth and seat; here the gift is given in person at Shrirangam.
  13. Mahaprabhu's prediction about Srinivasa, given to Gopala Bhatta at Shrirangam, is also known from the Prema-vilasa and the Bhakti-ratnakara (cf. ev-gosvamis-foresee-srinivasa); the "seat and cord" are the seat (asana) and cord sent by Mahaprabhu to Gopala Bhatta, now worshipped in the Radha-ramana temple.
  14. CC Adi 10.105.
  15. The Gopala-bhattashtaka, attributed to Krishnadasa Kaviraja; the edition has five verses, the text is corrupt in places — translated by sense. The payar paraphrase (147–159) precedes the verses themselves.
  16. The Hari-bhakti-vilasa is named in its colophons as a work of Gopala Bhatta, although tradition attributes the main text or the commentary to Sanatana; the author explains this by the "non-difference of bodies" of the two Gosvamis.
  17. The author attributes the verse to the Vaishnava-toshani; it has not been identified in the known text of that commentary.
  18. The same verse as 1.3.
  19. The Vaishnava-vandana of Daivakinandana Dasa (16th–17th c.).
